newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fujitsu to invest 150 bln yen in new chip plant.
newsitem.headline: Fujitsu to invest 150 bln yen in new chip plant.

text.p: Fujitsu Ltd said on Wednesday that it would invest 150 billion yen to build a new semiconductor plant in northern Japan.
It said the plant would use 0.18 micron technology to produce memory and logic LSI products.
The plant would be built in Aizu-Wakamatsu in Fukushima Prefecture, Fujitsu said in a statement.
Construction will start during the first half of the year from April 1, 1998 and operations will start in the second half of the year from April 1, 1999, the company said.

The plant, which will accommodate 0.18 micron production technology and 12-inch wafers, would produce both random access memory (RAM) and logic products using advanced mixed-line production techniques, Fujitsu said.
The facility would be capable of producing 256 megabit to one gigabit dynamic random access memories (DRAMs), it said.

The investment is the first phase of the new plant and Fujitsu would consider expansion in the future, a company spokeswoman said, adding, however, that the firm had no specific plan yet for a second phase of the plant.
